newsitem.title: FRANCE: Congo president wants African force in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Congo president wants African force in Zaire.

text.p: Congolese President Pascal Lissouba said in an interview on Wednesday an African peace force should be sent to Zaire.

"An African force must intervene in Zaire where Africa must play the main role (in bringing peace), even if the logistical support comes from outside the continent," he told the daily newspaper Le Parisien.
Lissouba gave the interview as African leaders met in the Togo capital, Lome, for a one-day summit on the crisis in Zaire where rebels are slowly gaining on the capital Kinshasa.
"As long as the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity don't wake up and give us the necessary logistical support, the idea of an inter-African peace force will not advance," he said.
Lissouba said those African leaders who backed the idea had asked France for logistical support. "The answer was not negative but Paris must take into account the opinion of its allies."
France, which backs ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, had long sought armed international intervention in Zaire but the idea was effectively vetoed by the United States.
Mobutu's camp has signalled it was ready to deal with Laurent Kabila's rebels, who have made short shrift of Zaire's ragged army in a five-month campaign.
The potential break-up of Africa's third biggest country, with nine neighbours, is a nightmare diplomats want to avoid.
More than 1,000 American, French and Belgian troops are massed in the Congo, one of those neighbours, ready to evacuate Westerners from Zaire if necessary.
